informant.nameEnglish: Duncan MacLennan and D. J. MacLennan

item.description: [kɾɑ̃ṉɔɡ] Quot.: “Cuir a-nall na [kɾɑ̃ṉɔɡs].” Note: the hooks which were put on a basket of herring for lifting out of the hold.
[ʃtʹe:lʹɑṉ] Quot.: “Shlaod a’ laogh a’ stéillean as a bhalla.” Note: a wooden or iron bar fixed on to wall of a byre, and to which a cow’s or calf’s neck rope was fixed.
Note: a hobble which was sometimes put on hens. String between two legs.
Quot.: “a’ cur cas-bheag air cù”. Note: one of a dog’s front paws in a sling hanging from its neck. To prevent it from straying too far.
[ɡibɑɡ] Quot.: “gibeag arbhair”. Note: a sheaf.
[kɾɔ:kɑn] Note: implement for digging up potatoes. Had a wooden handle with an iron hook on the end. Also an earmark:
[ɫu̜:d̪əɡɑṉ] Note: hinge on a door of this type –
Quot.: “Tha i a’ togail a chabhadh-mara.”
[ˈkɫɛəvɑṉ] Note: locking device put on the inside of a door.
Quot.: “The éirigh as a’ mhuir.” Note: There is a swell on the sea.
Quot.: “fiacail na h-eathar”. Note: the junction or joint between the stempost and keel.
[t̪ɤilʹe:vi] Note: a village meeting-hall.
Quot.: “Thàinig an t-inneadh orm.” Note: when weaving, if extra yarn is needed for weft to finish the tweed.
[ʃwsəkɔt̪] Note: a dress waistcoat as in a three-piece suit.
Note: fisherman’s jersey.
Note: bridesmaid.
Quot.: “Co bha a’ comhailteachadh?” Note: when a newly-married couple went to church together for the first time.
[mɔ̃ṉɑʃɑx] Note: having an easy-oasy, couldn’t-care-less attitude.
[lʹu̟ɡɑx] Note: shy.
Note: sneaky. Also used of a very slow-spoken person. (Also slìogaire.)
Note: tall and thin.
[bɾɑxilʹə] Note: a gluttonous person.
[ɡʹɑ:rtʹɑx] Note: witty.
[dɾɤ:ɡɑn̪t̪ə] Note: dogged, persevering, determined. Often used of a good worker, someone who is always at something.
Quot.: “Meall is caith e ’s cuir a-nall an ath-aodach.” Note: said to one who has just bought or got new clothes.
[rɑsɡə] Note: an eyelash.
[mɛ̃ləṉ] Note: eyebrows.
[rɤ̃ĩnʹ] Note: hair parting.
[kɑɾɑbəʴsḏ] Quot.: “Tha carbard math fhiaclan ann.” [NOTES: the turned r used for the symbol which is unclear in the original.]

[kɑmrɑicɑx] Quot.: “duine camraiceach”. Note: troublesome person, always stirring up trouble. [NOTES: note added by Professor Roibeard Ó Maolalaigh (RÓM) next to the second [ɑ] in the transcription – OK?]
[kũ̟məðıɡʹɑx] Quot.: “’S e aite cumruigeach a th’ann.” Note: an out-of-the-way place.
